edges.description: Lower blood hemoglobin reflects cumulative intra-alveolar blood loss and functional sequestration of erythrocyte-derived iron inside alveolar macrophages.
Decreased circulating iron reports functional systemic iron deficiency due to inability of alveolar macrophages to recycle pulmonary hemosiderin back to the bone marrow.
Decreased transferrin saturation and elevated total iron-binding capacity indicate systemic iron deficiency despite abundant pulmonary hemosiderin stores.
Preserved serum ferritin in the setting of low serum iron and microcytic anemia reflects macrophage hemosiderin storage in the lungs, whereas low ferritin prompts evaluation for celiac malabsorption.
Elevated reticulocyte count reflects active erythroid regeneration in response to ongoing pulmonary hemorrhage.
Elevated serum bilirubin from intra-alveolar heme degradation is significantly more frequent in children with recurrent IPH than in those who achieve sustained improvement.
Detection of SMA, ANCA, ANA, or celiac disease autoantibodies identifies patients with immune dysregulation or Lane-Hamilton syndrome.
